title: Stand on type’s shoulders
principle: Before inventing decorative lettering, study existing type anatomy and historical forms so invention is informed—not accidental.
procedure: Identify the genre (script, display sans, slab) and 3 historical references.
Trace or redraw a reference to learn its rhythm.
List non-negotiable anatomy rules for that genre.
Only then invent a twist that still obeys the rules.
examplePrompts:
Prepare a lettering brief grounded in type history.

Genre: <…>
3 references + what we learn from each.
Anatomy rules we will not break.
One intentional twist.
 crediting note for process doc.
tips: Hische’s craft is rooted in deep type literacy made public.
